Hermitian matrix model (Z=∫dMe−S(M))

Words: 179 Articles: 2
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A Hermitian matrix model replaces a spacetime field by a finite-dimensional Hermitian matrix. Its normalized integral supplies correlation functions and a zero-dimensional perturbative quantum field theory expansion. For an action built from traces of matrix powers, unitary matrix conjugation is a symmetry and the eigenvalues describe the invariant degrees of freedom. A quartic real integral needs a nonnegative highest-order coupling for convergence; a formal power series can be studied independently of this convergence issue.

Matrix diagonalization ghost determinant (det′addiagλ​∝∏i<j​(λi​−λj​)2)

Words: 64
Hermitian matrix model OurBigBook.com
Imposing vanishing off-diagonal entries with auxiliary integrations and an off-diagonal Grassmann Gaussian integral gives a determinant of the commutator map on the off-diagonal matrix units. Its eigenvalues are λi​−λj​, i=j. Up to a constant sign, their product is the squared Vandermonde determinant. It contributes −2∑i<j​log∣λi​−λj​∣ to the eigenvalue action, encoding repulsion between distinct eigenvalues. Diagonal zero modes and constant normalization factors must be treated separately.

Quartic Hermitian matrix two-point function (⟨Mij​Mkl​⟩c​)

Words: 53
Hermitian matrix model OurBigBook.com
For S=atr(M2)/2+btr(M4)/4 with a>0, the Wick theorem gives
⟨Mij​Mkl​⟩c​=a1​δil​δkj​−a3b​(2Nδil​δkj​+δij​δkl​)+O(b2).
(1)
There are eight adjacent external-attachment contractions with one free matrix-index sum and four opposite attachments with no free sum. The second tensor structure is needed at finite N; omitting it is an additional large-N approximation, not merely restricting to connected Feynman diagrams.

Radiative correction

Words: 34
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A radiative correction is a quantum correction beyond the classical or tree approximation, represented in perturbative quantum field theory by Feynman diagrams of positive loop order. Such corrections can alter a scalar potential and its derivatives; symmetries and renormalization constrain which changes are allowed.

Perturbation series

Words: 69 Articles: 1
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A perturbation series expands a correlation function or scattering amplitude in powers of interaction couplings. In quantum field theory it is commonly asymptotic because diagram counts grow factorially and nonperturbative effects are invisible to every finite order.

Weak coupling

Words: 32
Perturbation series OurBigBook.com
Weak coupling means a suitably dimensionless interaction strength is small. In BCS theory, νs​V≪1 gives a gap exponentially small compared with the pairing-shell energy cutoff; the expansion parameter is not the dimensional quantity V alone.

Differentiation of the Dyson time-ordered exponential (i∂t​U=HI​(t)U)

Words: 84
Dyson series OurBigBook.com
For bounded norm-continuous Hamiltonian operators on [t0​,t], the Dyson series has an n-th term bounded by Mn∣t−t0​∣n/n!, so it converges in operator norm. In its nested-integral form, differentiating the outer endpoint puts HI​(t) on the left of the (n−1)-fold term. Summing yields ∂t​U=−iHI​(t)U and U(t0​,t0​)=I. If HI​ is Hermitian, differentiating U†U proves unitarity. For unbounded field operators the same algebra is a formal perturbative identity unless domain and convergence assumptions or a regulator justify the steps. Evolution backward uses inverse, anti-time-ordered evolution.

Wick's theorem

Words: 1k Articles: 22
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Wick theorem expresses a time-ordered product of free fields as its normal-ordered product plus the sum over every possible contraction. It turns the Dyson series into Feynman diagrams.

Two-field Wick contraction identity (Tϕ(x)ϕ(y)=:ϕ(x)ϕ(y):+DF​(x−y))

Words: 53
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Split a free scalar field into its annihilation and creation parts. For x0>y0, changing the product into normal ordering adds [ϕ(+)(x),ϕ(−)(y)], the positive-frequency two-point function. For the opposite ordering interchange the two points. Their combination is the Feynman propagator, equal to the vacuum expectation of the time-ordered product. Iterating this identity gives the scalar Wick theorem.

Two-field scalar Wick identity (T{ϕ(x)ϕ(y)}=:ϕ(x)ϕ(y):+ΔF​(x−y)1)

Words: 47
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
For a free real scalar field, split ϕ=ϕ(+)+ϕ(−) into annihilation and creation parts. Moving the creation operators left gives ϕ(x)ϕ(y)=:ϕ(x)ϕ(y):+[ϕ(+)(x),ϕ(−)(y)]. The commutator is the Wightman function. Choosing either time order gives the displayed identity with the Feynman propagator. It is an identity of operator-valued distributions; coincident-point products need a suitable prescription.

Inductive proof of the scalar Wick theorem

Words: 125
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Split each free real scalar field as ϕ=ϕ(−)+ϕ(+), into creation and annihilation parts. For chronologically ordered arguments, the first field has the latest time. Multiplying it into a normal-ordered product of the remaining fields gives
ϕ1​:∏r∈I​ϕr​:=:ϕ1​∏r∈I​ϕr​:+∑j∈I​[ϕ1(+)​,ϕj(−)​]:∏r∈I∖{j}​ϕr​:.
(3)
This follows by commuting the annihilation part through each creation part; each commutator is a scalar, and all creation parts commute among themselves, as do all annihilation parts. The scalar commutator is the Feynman propagator for the chronological pair. Induction on the number of fields therefore lists every partial pairing exactly once: either field 1 remains unpaired or it pairs with one j. This proves the Wick theorem for free bosonic fields, including the empty pairing. Vacuum expectation retains only complete pairings. The identities are understood for regulated or smeared operator-valued distributions.

Free scalar four-point function (⟨Tϕ1​ϕ2​ϕ3​ϕ4​⟩)

Words: 44
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
For a centered free real scalar field, its vacuum time-ordered product has expectation ⟨Tϕ1​ϕ2​ϕ3​ϕ4​⟩=G12​G34​+G13​G24​+G14​G23​, where Gij​ is the Feynman propagator between insertions i,j. These are the three complete pairings in the Wick theorem. All remaining normal-ordered products have zero vacuum expectation. No fermionic interchange signs occur for a bosonic field.

Vanishing odd correlators of a free Gaussian field (⟨f​1​⋯f​2n+1​⟩=0)

Words: 55
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
A centered free field in a Gaussian vacuum has only pair contractions, so every odd correlator vanishes by Wick theorem. Equivalently, number parity reverses the field while preserving the vacuum. This statement applies to smeared or regulated fields; it does not assert that unregulated coincident products exist. Interactions or a nonzero field mean can invalidate it.

Time ordering

Words: 261 Articles: 5
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Time ordering places operators with later time arguments to the left. Interchanging fermionic operators also contributes the sign of the required permutation.

Fermionic time ordering (T[A(x)B(y)]=θ(x0−y0)A(x)B(y)−θ(y0−x0)B(y)A(x))

Words: 42
Time ordering OurBigBook.com
For two odd fermionic operators, time ordering contributes a minus sign whenever the chronological rearrangement exchanges them. For several fields the sign is the sign of a permutation restricted to the odd fields. This convention makes the free Dirac propagator a Green function of the Dirac equation with its contact term fixed by the canonical anticommutation relations.

Time-ordered exponential (U(t,t0​)=Texp[−i∫t0​t​H(s)ds/ℏ])

Words: 158 Articles: 2
Time ordering OurBigBook.com
The time-ordered exponential solves iℏ∂t​U=H(t)U with initial condition U(t0​,t0​)=I. Its expansion is the Dyson series. For bounded continuous Hamiltonian operators the series converges, as in differentiation of the Dyson time-ordered exponential. If the generators commute at all times, time ordering is unnecessary and an ordinary operator exponential suffices.
Magnus expansion (U(T)=exp(Ω1​+Ω2​+⋯))
Words: 73
Time-ordered exponential OurBigBook.com
For U˙=A(t)U and U(0)=I, the Magnus expansion writes the logarithm of the propagator as iterated integrals of commutators. Its first terms are Ω1​=∫0T​A(t)dt and Ω2​=21​∫0T​dt∫0t​ds[A(t),A(s)]. For a Quantum Hamiltonian, A=−iH/ℏ, so a noncommuting time-dependent control has corrections beyond the exponential of its integrated Quantum Hamiltonian. This formula is a local convergent expansion under suitable smallness conditions, or a formal expansion; it must not be assumed globally convergent for arbitrary pulse durations.
Constant pulse-axis condition for removing time ordering ([H(t),H(s)]=0⟹U(T)=e−i∫0T​H(t)dt/ℏ)
Words: 44
Time-ordered exponential OurBigBook.com
For H(t)=Ω1​(t)A+Ω2​(t)B with fixed noncommuting Hermitian operators, [H(t),H(s)]=[Ω1​(t)Ω2​(s)−Ω2​(t)Ω1​(s)][A,B]. A constant ratio of the envelopes is sufficient to remove time ordering. Independently changing that ratio generally produces commutator corrections in the Magnus expansion, and a product of successive pulses need not equal the exponential of their summed areas.

Time-ordered product (T{O1​⋯On​})

Words: 39
Time ordering OurBigBook.com
A time-ordered product sorts operator insertions from latest time on the left to earliest time on the right. Reordering odd fermionic operators contributes the sign of their permutation. For bosonic A,B, T[A(t)B(t′)]=θ(t−t′)A(t)B(t′)+θ(t′−t)B(t′)A(t). Vacuum expectations of free time-ordered products are evaluated by the Wick theorem.

Normal ordering

Words: 432 Articles: 7
Wick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Normal ordering places creation operators to the left of annihilation operators. For free fields it removes vacuum self-contractions from a composite operator.

Normal-ordering subtraction scheme in two dimensions (VB​=e−TΛ​∂ϕ2​/2V)

Words: 84
Normal ordering OurBigBook.com
For a massive real scalar field in two spacetime dimensions with a polynomial potential and no derivative interactions, every connected subgraph has superficial degree of divergence ω=2(1−V), where V counts interaction vertices. The only divergent loop subgraphs with external legs have one vertex and consist of self-contractions. Normal ordering removes them. Renormalization of spontaneously broken gauge theories

Words: 975 Articles: 3
Renormalization OurBigBook.com
Renormalization of spontaneously broken gauge theories means that the Higgs mechanism can generate gauge boson masses while a fixed finite set of renormalized couplings, masses and field normalizations still suffices to absorb ultraviolet divergences. The symmetry constrains the counterterms even when the chosen vacuum expectation value hides it. This makes radiative corrections to the electroweak interaction calculable after inputs have been fixed by renormalization conditions.
A useful distinction is between choosing variables that display the physical particles and choosing variables that display good power counting. Unitary gauge removes the would-be Goldstone bosons from the explicit fields. R-xi gauge keeps them and the required Faddeev-Popov ghosts in intermediate Feynman diagrams, exposing simpler large-momentum behavior. The physical scattering amplitude must agree after all contributions and counterterms have been included consistently.
In Renormalizable Lagrangians for massive Yang-Mills fields (1971), Gerard 't Hooft constructed spontaneously broken gauge theories with massive gauge bosons. His worked SU(2) gauge theory with an adjoint Higgs field leaves a massless photon; it is a demonstration model, not the full chiral Standard Model. The gauge fixing, Faddeev-Popov ghosts and Ward identities connect renormalizability with physical unitarity.[ref]
Regularization and renormalization of gauge fields (1972), by Gerard 't Hooft and Martinus J. G. Veltman, developed dimensional regularization with recursive subtraction of ultraviolet subdivergences. It continued Feynman integrals in the dimension, keeping the relevant Ward identities in non-anomalous cases; its final section examined quantum anomalies. The procedure does not make an inconsistent chiral gauge theory consistent: gauge anomaly cancellation remains essential.[ref]
The organizing proof outline is to use good large-momentum propagators, subtract every divergent subgraph, and constrain the remaining local divergences by the Ward identities. A finite family of allowed counterterms must close under this operation at every loop order. The same identities must remove unphysical intermediate contributions from physical amplitudes. Power counting alone establishes neither closure nor these cancellations. Modern BRST symmetry packages these restrictions; the scalar subtraction below illustrates only locality.

Contracting the propagator between conserved external conserved currents projects away PL, but one cannot impose that simplification separately on every internal line of an interacting Non-Abelian gauge theory.

From renormalizability to electroweak predictions

Words: 172
Renormalization of spontaneously broken gauge theories OurBigBook.com
The 1999 recognition of Gerard 't Hooft and Martinus J. G. Veltman concerned the theoretical quantum structure of the electroweak interaction.[ref] Renormalizability makes repeated radiative corrections predictive from a fixed set of inputs. It does not imply that the perturbation series converges, nor that renormalization alone chooses the correct particle content or excludes all physics beyond the Standard Model.
The Gargamelle collaboration prepared an experimental test by exposing its heavy-liquid bubble chamber to neutrino and antineutrino beams at CERN. The readout selected events producing hadrons without an identified muon or electron, compared with events containing a charged lepton. Its 1974 report assessed alternative origins from neutrons and long-lived neutral kaons, finding them insufficient to explain the sample. That supported neutral currents; it did not isolate a radiative correction or demonstrate renormalizability.[ref]
The distinction matters when using the tree-level electroweak gauge-boson masses:
mW​=mZ​cosθW​.
(22)
Beyond tree level, self-energies, interaction vertices and counterterms alter how chosen input observables predict another observable. The Weinberg angle then needs a specified renormalization scheme; inserting its value from one convention into a formula from another can create an apparent discrepancy. A meaningful higher-order test must state both its independent experimental inputs and the calculated loop order.

Asymptotic freedom
Words: 1k Articles: 8
Beta function (physics) OurBigBook.com
An asymptotically free theory has a running coupling that tends to zero at arbitrarily high energy. Its negative weak-coupling beta function makes short-distance perturbation theory increasingly accurate.
In Quantum chromodynamics, this means that a short-distance probe can resolve quarks with a small QCD coupling, even though isolated quarks are absent from the observed hadron spectrum. This made asymptotic freedom a bridge between the approximately free constituents of the parton model and an interacting quantum field theory. Asymptotic freedom supplies control at large momentum transfer; it does not itself prove confinement.[ref]
Use the four-dimensional QCD coupling convention αs​=gs2​/(4π). For the SU(3) gauge group and nf​ active quark flavors in the fundamental representation, the one-loop order beta function is
μdμdgs​​=−16π2β0​gs3​​+O(gs5​),β0​=11−32nf​​,dlnμ2dαs​​=−4πβ0​​αs2​+O(αs3​).
(27)
Here nf​ counts quark flavors, not the three values of color charge. The chain rule converts the first equation to the last; changing from lnμ to lnμ2 supplies a factor of two. For β0​>0, the negative sign makes gs​=0 an attractive high-energy renormalization-group fixed point.[ref]
For β0​>0, set the renormalization scale μ=Q, where Q is a positive energy scale. The one-loop running of the strong coupling then gives
αs​(Q)=β0​ln(Q2/Λ2)4π​.
(28)
The strong-coupling scale Λ has the same units of measurement as Q, so the logarithm has a dimensionless argument. This is a fixed-nf​ approximation on the positive branch Q>Λ; controlled perturbative quantum field theory requires a small QCD coupling and suitably small omitted corrections, not merely a positive denominator. Heavy quark masses require matching the QCD scale across a quark threshold, changing nf​ and the associated Λ. Both the renormalization scheme and the loop order matter when quoting a numerical Λ.

From deep inelastic scaling to asymptotic freedom
Words: 190
Asymptotic freedom OurBigBook.com
The 1969 SLAC-MIT deep inelastic electron scattering experiment found approximate Bjorken scaling: an estimated deep-inelastic structure function depended mainly on a ratio of kinematic variables. Its restricted angular coverage did not separately determine both deep-inelastic structure functions, and the extraction assumed transverse virtual photons. This was motivation for a microscopic theory, not already a measurement of the QCD coupling.[ref]
The 1973 David Gross–Frank Wilczek calculation supplied a quantum field theory explanation of approximately free partons with calculable logarithmic corrections. Asymptotic freedom therefore permits approximate Bjorken scaling without requiring exact scale independence. The QCD coupling governs the corrections, while parton distribution functions and their evolution connect the short-distance calculation to a proton.[ref]
In a later direct test, H1 collided Positrons and protons at HERA and selected deep inelastic scattering events. A liquid-argon particle calorimeter identified the outgoing Positron with an associated track; calorimeter deposits and charged tracks reconstructed particle jets in the Breit frame. Vertex, timing and longitudinal energy-balance cuts suppressed backgrounds; two simulations checked detector corrections. Fits of particle jet cross sections to next-to-leading-order QCD extracted αs​(ET​) in transverse-energy bins, consistent with decreasing QCD coupling. Hadronization, parton distribution functions and renormalization scale choices limited the inference. This measures rates and fits a coupling, rather than directly reading a force meter.[ref]
Discovery of asymptotic freedom and the 2004 Nobel Prize
Words: 126
Asymptotic freedom OurBigBook.com
David Gross and Frank Wilczek, and independently H. David Politzer, published their one-loop order Non-Abelian gauge theory results in adjacent 1973 Physical Review Letters papers. Both established a high-energy route to weak coupling; extrapolating into the low-energy region was a separate dynamical problem.[ref][ref]
The three shared the 2004 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering asymptotic freedom in the theory of the strong interaction. David Gross's Nobel lecture describes the unexpected sign and their comparison of independent calculations.[ref] In his lecture The Dilemma of Attribution, H. David Politzer emphasizes that the prize marks a wider community's work and that a tidy prize-centered history hides how discovery actually proceeds.[ref]

A zero superficial degree of divergence does not force divergence: gauge invariance can cancel the candidate local term. An ultraviolet subdivergence arises when loop momenta internal to a proper subgraph tend to infinity while the momenta entering that subgraph are held fixed. Recursive local counterterms subtract these subgraph divergences before the remaining overall divergence is analyzed. A tadpole diagram inserted into an otherwise convergent six-point phi-fourth theory Feynman diagram is a simple massive example.

Quantum electrodynamics (QED)

Words: 3k Articles: 49
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
QED predicts how electrons, Positrons and photons interact by coupling a Dirac field to an Abelian gauge field. For a field of signed electric charge qe​, the interaction is Lint​=−qe​ψˉ​γμψAμ​; an electron has qe​=−e, e>0. Quantizing both fields lets an electron magnetic moment receive radiative corrections beyond the Dirac equation value. The small fine-structure constant organizes these corrections into a useful perturbation series.
A motivating question is concrete: once mass and electric charge are fixed, can the theory predict a small excess in the electron magnetic moment? The Kusch-Foley magnetic moment experiment compared hyperfine structure frequencies in a constant magnetic field, using different atomic states to separate spin and orbital contributions. Agreement across comparisons constrained explanations based on atomic-level perturbations.[ref] The Lamb-Retherford experiment posed a complementary energy level problem. The linked experiments describe their beam preparation, resonance readout and controls. Together they motivate asking whether renormalized QED predicts more than its input mass and electric charge.

Finite precision tests of the leading electron anomaly

Words: 190
Schwinger correction to the electron magnetic moment OurBigBook.com
A prediction becomes useful when its error and the competing models are explicit. Consider an original hypothetical readout a∗​=0.00116 with stipulated absolute tolerance 2×10−5. Hold the teaching input α=1/137 fixed. Compare three models: the Dirac equation baseline ae​=0, the leading QED value ae​=α/(2π), and a trial coefficient twice as large, ae​=α/π. Their absolute residuals are respectively 0.00116, approximately 1.7149×10−6, and approximately 0.00116343. Only the leading QED value lies inside this stipulated tolerance. The example tests both the existence and the size of a correction; it does not quote an actual observation or assign the tolerance a statistical interpretation.
At tighter precision, including more loop orders and propagating the uncertainty in the fine-structure constant becomes essential. The first omitted term has order α2, but the order symbol alone gives no numerical error bound. If α changes by a small δα, this leading prediction changes by δae​=δα/(2π). Thus a comparison must state which input determined α: extracting it from the very electron magnetic moment being tested would not supply an independent test of that input. Agreement with one leading term at one tolerance does not establish agreement to arbitrarily many digits.

For tree electron-Positron annihilation into three photons, all six orders along the fermion line must be summed. Write D(r)=r−m and S(r)=D(r)−1=(r+m)/(r2−m2). Contracting an internal photon with its momentum gives S(R)qS(r)=S(R)−S(r) when q=r−R. Contracting an end photon removes its adjacent Dirac propagator by the external Dirac equation, with a minus sign at the electron end and a plus sign at the positron end. For either fixed order of the two uncontracted photons, the three insertion positions therefore telescope to zero. Summing their two orders proves the Ward identity. The mass terms in both remaining Dirac propagators are essential when m=0. The result expresses the invariance of the scattering amplitude under ϵℓ​↦ϵℓ​+cqℓ​.

Proper-vertex Ward-Takahashi identity in QED (kμ​Γμ(p+k,p)=S−1(p+k)−S−1(p))

Define the proper electromagnetic vertex with the electric charge removed, and define S−1 without the propagator's overall factor i. The displayed off-shell identity follows by localizing the vector symmetry in a time-ordered correlation function, including the contact terms at the charged-field insertions, and amputating. Its on-shell form gives the Ward identity for physical photon amplitudes. At zero photon momentum it identifies the vertex with the momentum derivative of the inverse fermion propagator.

In a gauge-preserving regularization and consistent renormalization convention, the proper-vertex Ward-Takahashi identity in QED equates the vertex and electron wave-function renormalization constants. With ψ0​=Z21/2​ψ and A0​=Z31/2​A, the vertex coefficient gives e0​=μRϵ​Z1​e/(Z2​Z3​​), proving the displayed charge relation in d=4−2ϵ. Gauge invariance restricts counterterms but does not forbid charge running.

Two-photon fermion Ward identity

Words: 64
Ward identity OurBigBook.com
The two photon orders in a tree-level charged-fermion amplitude must be summed. Contracting one photon vertex with its momentum writes the contracted slash as a difference of inverse Dirac propagators. The external Dirac equations remove the on shell inverse factors; the two remaining terms have equal size and opposite sign. Thus the sum vanishes under the momentum replacement although individual diagrams generally do not. This implements the gauge equivalence of photon polarization vectors.

Power counting in quantum field theory

Words: 653 Articles: 14
Perturbative quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Power counting assigns mass dimensions to fields and couplings. An interaction is relevant, marginal or irrelevant when its coupling has positive, zero or negative mass dimension, respectively.

Truncation error in effective field theory

Words: 46
Power counting in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The truncation error in effective field theory is the uncertainty from omitted orders of a stated energy, derivative or loop expansion. It is commonly estimated from the first omitted terms using an explicit assumption about Wilson coefficients. Small energy alone does not justify ignoring an anomalously large coupling or a nearby omitted pole.

Mass dimension ([X])

Words: 141 Articles: 2
Power counting in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
In units with ℏ=c=1, the mass dimension [X] is the exponent with which a quantity scales under a common rescaling of energies and momenta. In d spacetime dimensions a Lagrangian density has mass dimension d.

Critical dimension of a monomial scalar interaction (Dc​=2n/(n−2))

Words: 51
Mass dimension OurBigBook.com
With a canonical kinetic term, a real scalar field has mass dimension (D−2)/2. A coupling constant multiplying ϕn therefore has mass dimension D−n(D−2)/2. For n>2, it is dimensionless precisely at Dc​=2n/(n−2), giving six for a cubic interaction and four for a quartic interaction. This is a power counting statement about perturbation theory, not a claim that the corresponding quantum beta function vanishes.

Engineering dimensions of relativistic fields ([ϕ]=(d−2)/2,[ψ]=(d−1)/2,[Aμ​]=(d−2)/2)

Words: 53
Mass dimension OurBigBook.com
Canonical free scalar and gauge-vector kinetic terms contain two derivatives and two fields, whereas the Dirac kinetic term contains one derivative and two spinor fields. Matching their mass dimension to d in d spacetime dimensions gives the displayed engineering dimensions. These are the dimensions used in power counting; interacting scaling dimensions can additionally contain anomalous contributions.

Superficial degree of divergence (D)

Words: 358 Articles: 5
Power counting in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The superficial degree of divergence D is the ultraviolet power predicted by rescaling all independent loop momenta together. For a scalar graph with L loops and I propagators behaving as p−2 in d dimensions, D=dL−2I before cancellations and subdivergences are considered.

Superficial degree of divergence OurBigBook.com
For a connected amputated Feynman diagram with the quartic Yukawa interaction in three spacetime dimensions, scalar quartic and scalar sextic vertices, b external bosonic legs, f external fermionic legs and n4​ scalar quartic vertices, the superficial degree of divergence is the displayed expression. Indeed ω=3L−2Ib​−If​, 2Ib​+b=2nY​+4n4​+6n6​, 2If​+f=2nY​ and L=Ib​+If​−nY​−n4​−n6​+1. Substitution eliminates the counts of the two marginal vertices. The bound concerns overall ultraviolet divergence, before numerator cancellations and subtraction of ultraviolet subdivergences.

Monomial scalar interaction power-counting identity (Δ=d−(d−2)E/2−[λ]V)

Words: 61
Superficial degree of divergence OurBigBook.com
For a connected scalar graph with nonderivative interaction −λϕn, E external legs and V vertices, nV=2I+E and L=I−V+1. Since [ϕ]=(d−2)/2 and [λ]=d−n(d−2)/2, the superficial degree of divergence is
Δ=dL−2I=d−2d−2​E−[λ]V.
(37)
The graph contributes at order λV. This is simultaneous large-loop-momentum counting for an amputated graph; it does not test subdivergences or guarantee that the predicted pole coefficient is nonzero.

A superficially convergent graph can have a divergent subgraph

Words: 69
Superficial degree of divergence OurBigBook.com
In massive four-dimensional phi-fourth theory, a six-point triangle is one-particle irreducible and has superficial degree −2. Insert a tadpole diagram self-energy into one of its internal lines. The resulting graph is still one-particle irreducible and still has degree −2, but its tadpole loop diverges. Recursive local counterterms remove the subgraph divergence before overall power counting is applied. Convergence requires attention to all ultraviolet subgraphs, not merely to simultaneous scaling of all loop momenta.

Derivative-interaction scalar power counting (D=d−(d−2)E/2−V[λ])

Words: 56
Superficial degree of divergence OurBigBook.com
For interaction λΦn(∂Φ)r with a two-derivative kinetic term, each vertex has n+r legs and r momentum powers. Since [Φ]=(d−2)/2, its coupling has dimension [λ]=d−(n+r)(d−2)/2−r. The graph identities 2I+E=(n+r)V and L=I−V+1, inserted into D=dL−2I+rV, prove the displayed formula. It is an upper bound on ultraviolet scaling; momentum contractions and symmetry can cause cancellations.

Scalar graph power-counting identity (D=d−(d/2−1)E−∑n​[n−d(n/2−1)]Vn​)

Words: 70
Superficial degree of divergence OurBigBook.com
For a connected scalar field theory graph without derivative vertices, each independent loop momentum supplies d powers and each internal scalar propagator removes two. Thus D=dL−2I. The graph identities L=I−∑n​Vn​+1 and 2I+E=∑n​nVn​ give the displayed formula. The mass dimension of the field is (d−2)/2 and that of gn​ is n−d(n/2−1). Negative-dimensional couplings allow the superficial degree to grow with vertex count. This is overall power counting in quantum field theory; subgraphs can diverge even when the whole graph has negative degree.

Marginal coupling

Words: 20
Power counting in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A marginal coupling is dimensionless under classical power counting.
The marginal interaction coefficient is distinct from the operator it multiplies.

Relevant coupling

Words: 14
Power counting in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A relevant coupling has positive mass dimension and grows under scaling toward long distances.

Irrelevant coupling

Words: 47 Articles: 1
Power counting in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
An irrelevant coupling has negative mass dimension and is suppressed toward long distances.

Nonrenormalizable interaction

Words: 34
Irrelevant coupling OurBigBook.com
A power-counting nonrenormalizable interaction has a coupling of negative mass dimension, so higher loop orders generally require counterterms of unbounded operator dimension. It is naturally interpreted within an effective field theory below a cutoff.
